concepts.def: Extremely high inflation, usually >50% per month.
Cost firms face changing prices frequently.
Time/effort wasted trying to spend cash fast.

walkthroughs.body_html: Weimar Germany (1923): prices doubled every few days; workers were paid twice a day. Zimbabwe 2008: a Z$100 trillion note circulated. Triggered by uncontrolled money printing. Cure: new currency, fiscal discipline, central bank credibility.

BoE raises Bank Rate → borrowing falls → AD slows → inflation eases. Government may also cut spending (fiscal tightening). Trade-off: slower growth, higher unemployment. Time lag of 12–18 months means caution.
Consider: cause (cost-push vs demand-pull responds to different policies), magnitude, expectations, side-effects on growth and jobs. Conclude with a judgement on the best policy mix in context.
